result: No unresolved substantive correction within the checked scope.
identityFindings: Boii is clearly the northern Italian record, with an explicit warning that the imported interval ends before the later archaeological examples and 191 BCE conquest. Etruscan writing at a mixed settlement is identified as Etruscan, not invented Gaulish.

Boihaenum is explicitly an uncertain imported label inferred to relate to Boiohaemum. Public prose warns that its eastern Moravian/Slovak outline poorly matches the proposed Bohemian core and rejects a continuous kingdom to 300 CE. Salač supports uncertain borders, northern Bohemian core and temporary alliances. Examples are geographically named, and Roman installations and Latin are expressly Roman rather than native Marcomannic facilities or speech.

Únětice is treated as a regionally varied archaeological culture. Pömmelte house, diet and vessel evidence is kept separate from earlier Bell Beaker and Corded Ware phases. No invented language or single-kingdom ending is supplied.
